newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bourse end down, UAP takeover talk returns.
newsitem.headline: French bourse end down, UAP takeover talk returns.

text.p: French stocks finished marginally weaker on Wednesday after five days on the rise, with talk of an offer for insurer UAP providing spark in the closing minutes and carmaker Renault falling further on gloomy predictions.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 4.06 points or 0.2 percent at 2,038.06, while the CAC-40 futures contract ended off 2.0 points at 2045.0 from Tuesday's close. Volume was a solid 4.68 billion francs.
Traders reported a late block trade of 250,000 shares in insurer Union des Assurances de Paris and market talk of an offer for the group, with Axa as predator. Axa denied the market rumour.
"Axa denies the rumours, according to which it is making a public offer for UAP," an Axa spokeswoman said.

Renault marked the biggest loss of the day after reporting poor first-half results on Tuesday and predicting on Wednesday that it could end the year in the red on the grounds cost-cuts would fail to offset price war pressures on margins.
The stock ended down 5.04 percent at 113 francs but off day's low. Fellow carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen weakened in sympathy to end off 10 francs at 559, or down 1.76 percent.
